Interface MessagePort

All Superinterfaces:
AutoCloseable
All Known Implementing Classes:
AbstractMessagePort, AtLeastOncePort, ExactlyOncePort, FireAndForgetPort, InMemoryMessagePort
public interface MessagePort extends AutoCloseable
A messaging port for sending and receiving COBOL records over any transport.

MessagePort abstracts the messaging substrate — JMS, IBM MQ, ZeroMQ, Kafka, MQTT, or raw sockets — behind a record-oriented interface. Messages are byte buffers that map directly to Record layouts (from copybooks), with optional EBCDIC translation for mainframe interop.

Three delivery semantics are supported via MessagePort.Delivery:

  • FIRE_AND_FORGET �� best effort, no acknowledgement (MQTT QoS 0, UDP)
  • AT_LEAST_ONCE — acknowledged delivery, may duplicate (MQTT QoS 1, JMS AUTO_ACKNOWLEDGE)
  • EXACTLY_ONCE — transactional, no loss or duplication (JMS SESSION_TRANSACTED, Kafka exactly-once)
// Send a record as a message
try (MessagePort port = SomePort.connect("queue://ORDERS")) {
    port.send(orderRecord);
}

// Receive and process
try (MessagePort port = SomePort.connect("queue://ORDERS")) {
    port.receive(orderRecord, rec -> {
        String orderId = rec.getString("ORDER-ID").trim();
        Decimal amount = rec.getDecimal("ORDER-AMOUNT");
        // process...
    });
}

    • receive

      boolean receive(Record record)
      Receive the next message, loading it into the provided Record. Blocks until a message is available or the port is closed.
      Parameters:
      record - the record to load the message into
      Returns:
      true if a message was received, false if the port closed

    • receive

      byte[] receive()
      Receive the next message as raw bytes. Returns null if the port closed before a message arrived.

    • receive

      boolean receive(Record record, long timeoutMs)
      Receive the next message with a timeout.
      Parameters:
      record - the record to load into
      timeoutMs - maximum time to wait in milliseconds (0 = non-blocking)
      Returns:
      true if a message was received, false on timeout or close

    • listen

      void listen(Record record, Consumer<Record> listener)
      Start a message listener — incoming messages are dispatched to the consumer. The Record is reused for each message (COBOL-style single-record-area).
      Parameters:
      record - the record to load each message into
      listener - callback for each received message

    • stopListening

      void stopListening()
      Stop listening for messages (if a listener is active).

    • acknowledge

      void acknowledge()
      Acknowledge the last received message (for AT_LEAST_ONCE and EXACTLY_ONCE). For FIRE_AND_FORGET, this is a no-op.

    • commit

      void commit()
      Commit the current messaging transaction (for EXACTLY_ONCE). For other delivery modes, this is a no-op.

    • rollback

      void rollback()
      Rollback the current messaging transaction (for EXACTLY_ONCE). The message will be redelivered.
